 Print A’ja Wilson turns Game 2 fan clash into fuel as 36 point performance sends Indiana Fever out of playoffs A’ja Wilson has added another major achievement to her career, winning a record fifth WNBA MVP award in 2026. However, three-time MVP Sheryl Swoopes believes calling someone the greatest player of all time (GOAT) is not that simple. Speaking on The Draymond Green Show on YouTube, Swoopes explained why comparing players from different generations can be unfair. Her comments come after Wilson became the first player in WNBA history to win three straight MVP awards, even as the Las Vegas Aces’ title defense ended in a semifinal sweep. Sheryl Swoopes Explains Why Comparing A’ja Wilson With Past WNBA Greats Is Difficult
 Swoopes, a three-time Olympic gold medalist, believes the GOAT debate often misses an important point: players from different eras did not have the same opportunities. She brought up Cheryl Miller, a college basketball legend who never played in the WNBA, to explain why judging greatness across generations can be difficult. On Friday’s episode of The Draymond Green Show , Swoopes said, “You know, my thing with that conversation is when people are like, oh, you’re the goat, she’s the goat, he’s the goat, they’re the goat, who’s the goat? I don’t know if it’s fair to compare different generations.” She also explained why Michael Jordan is her personal GOAT in the NBA. Swoopes said she watched him play during her own time, making his achievements more meaningful to her. “Listen, Michael Jordan is my goat because I watched him play. Like, that was during my time… I just personally hate that conversation. I just do. Because I feel like you’re never going to get it right…,” she added. For Swoopes, choosing a personal favorite is different from claiming that one player is unquestionably better than everyone else. She compared the debate to picking a Mount Rushmore of basketball, where limiting the list to four names means leaving out other great players. Draymond Green agreed with her point. He also noted that fans cannot watch complete footage of every historic achievement, including Wilt Chamberlain’s famous 100-point NBA game. That makes comparisons between players from different periods even harder. A’ja Wilson’s Fifth MVP Adds More Weight to Her WNBA GOAT Case
 Wilson has a strong case for being part of the GOAT conversation. According to the WNBA’s official announcement, she received 713 points in the 2026 MVP voting, including 65 of the 74 first-place votes. Minnesota Lynx rookie Olivia Miles finished second with 442 points. The award was Wilson’s fifth overall, following wins in 2020, 2022, 2024 and 2025. She also became the first player in league history to win MVP three years in a row. Join conversation

 Wilson finished the 2026 regular season with 1,073 points, averaging 26.2 points per game. She also recorded 9.4 rebounds, 3.2 assists and 1.9 blocks per game. It was her second season with more than 1,000 points, making her the only player in WNBA history to achieve that feat more than once. Yet Wilson’s individual success could not prevent the Aces from falling short of another title. The Golden State Valkyries swept Las Vegas in the semifinals, winning Game 3 by 87-77 in overtime on October 9. Wilson also shared how much the MVP award meant to her beyond basketball. Reflecting on her younger self, she said, “That’s why I cried harder on this one because 15-year-old A’ja wasn’t sitting up here dreaming about being a five-time MVP. She wasn’t dreaming about being a three-time champion. She was dreaming about surviving this world.” Her words offered a personal look at the journey behind her records. While Wilson’s achievements will keep her name in the GOAT debate, Swoopes’ argument shows why there may never be one answer that satisfies everyone.
